messages:
pagerduty: PAGER: maya rao on-call (severity: P1) -> api-gateway errors spike in eu-west-1. Please acknowledge. :rotating_light:

maya rao: acked. I'm looking. seeing 502/504 spike on /v1/generate from edge nodes -> 503 on a few LB health checks. Metrics: 5xx rate ~18% for the last 3 min, p95 latency jumped from 120ms -> 2.6s.

infra-bot: alert: high-error-rate on service=api-gateway env=prod region=eu-west-1 (5xx > 15% for 3m).

ben chen: @maya any recent deploys?

maya rao: nothing deployed in eu region in the last hour per deploy-bot.

olivia park: I can pull logs and tail proxy error rates. give me a minute.

maya rao: oncall checklist: 1) confirm scope/impact 2) mitigation (route/fallback) 3) escalate if customer impact high 4) postmortem owner

olivia park: tailing nginx on edge-proxy-pool-7:
```
2026-03-15T14:01:12Z error upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header from upstream
2026-03-15T14:01:13Z 502 "upstream sent no data"
2026-03-15T14:02:01Z 504 "upstream timed out"
```

olivia park: pattern: rapid upstream connection closures across multiple proxies. headers show upstream=backend-internal:443 with TLS 1.3 handshake restarts.

sandeep kumar: checking LB and backend pool health. kubectl get pods -n gateway shows backend-internal has plenty of replicas and Ready=1. No OOM.

ben chen: are upstreams overloaded? what's active conn count?

maya rao: running a quick query -> grafana: connection_count to backend-internal jumped ~5x around spike start. also see retry queue growing.

olivia park: reproducing via curl from an edge host:
```
curl -v -H "Host: api.redwood.ai" https://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/generate
* Connected to 127.0.0.1 (127.0.0.1) port 8080 (#0)
> GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
> < HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
< Server: nginx/1.20.1
< Content-Type: text/html
< Content-Length: 146
< Connection: keep-alive
< \n* Connection #0 to host 127.0.0.1 left intact
```

maya rao: initial hypothesis: upstream (backend-internal) is dropping connections — possibly due to ephemeral port exhaustion on the egress side or a transient kernel TCP setting after a platform update. No deploy but there was an automated host kernel patch earlier today on a subset of edge hosts (reported by infra-bot at 06:00 UTC).

sandeep kumar: checking netstat on a sample host: ephemeral ports in use top out, SYN_RECV counts high. looks like TIME_WAIT and ephemeral exhaustion.

ben chen: can we enable connection pooling / keepalives to reduce churn? short-term mitigation: 1) spin up extra backend-internal replicas in eu-west-1 2) apply NAT port range bump on edge NAT nodes or reconfigure SNAT, 3) enable fallback route to regional-dedicated cluster for critical customers.

maya rao: do 1 & 3 now. ben, can you open a canary route to dedicated in eu? olivia, spin up 4 extra pods for backend-internal. sandeep, shotgun NAT port bump and restart NAT agent on a single host to test.

ben chen: running route change:
```
# using routing-service to add fallback for route /v1/generate
routing-cli create-fallback --from=api-gateway-eu --to=dedicated-eu --route=/v1/generate --weight=20
```

ben chen: fallback created and canary traffic at 20% -> health check green on dedicated target. observing error rate drop ~6%. :thumbsup:

olivia park: scaling backend-internal now:
```
kubectl scale deploy/backend-internal -n gateway --replicas=12
```

olivia park: new pods ready. connection_count per proxy dropping, 5xx down to ~7% after scale and canary.

sandeep kumar: applied ephemeral port bump to NAT (range 32768-61000 -> 32768-65535) and restarted nat-agent on 1 host. monitoring.

infra-bot: change recorded: nat-config update by sandeep kumar; host nat-agent restart performed (host=edge-17).

maya rao: rolling forward NAT change to remaining 3 edge NAT hosts in eu (staggered 30s) to avoid simultaneous restarts.

ben chen: we should also throttle retries from gateway for now to avoid amplification. updating gateway retry policy to backoff and jitter.

maya rao: applied temporary retry-policy change: retries=1, per-try-timeout=1s, jitter=true.

olivia park: error rate now ~2% and p95 latency back down to ~180ms. customer impact: looks limited to API calls that don't retry; about 12% of requests had error traces initially. we've cleared majority.

maya rao: notifying support and customers: posting incident notice to status page draft – small intermittent errors in EU region, mitigation in progress. tagging SLAs team for any impacted enterprise customers.

ben chen: any sign of a bad upstream version? logs show similar docker images across replicas, no crashloops.

sandeep kumar: NAT port bump across hosts complete. no host-level alerts.

maya rao: summary so far: cause likely ephemeral port exhaustion / connection churn after earlier kernel patch + high short-lived connections. mitigations: scaled backend-internal, enabled dedicated fallback (20% canary -> now 0% as we brought stable), bumped NAT ephemeral range and staggered restarts, reduced retries.

olivia park: follow-ups: 1) permanent NAT port range update and capacity increase 2) add more aggressive connection pooling / keepalive between gateway and backend 3) add metric alarms for ephemeral-port-utilization 4) postmortem owner: ben chen.

maya rao: assigning postmortem to @ben. keeping channel open for 15 more minutes to verify stability, then will archive. Great work team. :tada:
